newsitem.title: USA: UPS pilots group says would support strike.
newsitem.headline: UPS pilots group says would support strike.

text.p: Most United Parcel Service pilots will refuse to work in the event of a strike by package handlers and drivers at the company, the Independent Pilots Association (IPA) said on Sunday.

"In the event of a Teamsters strike, IPA members will perform no company duty of any kind. This includes no flying, training or company directed deadheading after the initiation of a strike," a telephone recording at IPA headquarters in Louisville, Ky., said.
Some 2,000 UPS pilots are members of the IPA.
In Atlanta, UPS spokesman Norman Black said that if IPA pilots did not show up for work, the company would try to maintain some level of air traffic by calling in 138 management-level pilots.

UPS flies out of 80 U.S. airports, and normally delivers 1.6 million packages a day by air. It has air hubs at Louisville, Ky.; Ontario, Calif.; Philadelphia; Columbia, S.C.; Dallas-Fort Worth, and Rockford, Ill.
UPS and union officials began last-minute talks in Washington late on Sunday to try to reach a deal on a new contract before a threatened union strike at midnight EDT (0400 GMT).
